edges.description: Without a functional beta subunit the IDH3 heterotetramer loses most of its catalytic activity and its affinity for NAD.
Loss of IDH3 activity slows the oxidation of isocitrate in mitochondria, so the metabolites upstream of the IDH3 step accumulate.
edges.target: Impaired Isocitrate Oxidation in the TCA Cycle

edges.description: Proposed but unproven step: reduced IDH3-dependent NADH generation is thought to leave photoreceptors, which already operate near their maximal mitochondrial respiratory capacity, with too little energetic reserve.
edges.source: Impaired Isocitrate Oxidation in the TCA Cycle

edges.description: Insufficient energy supply is the proposed cause of photoreceptor loss; the cell-death pathway in IDH3B-related retinopathy has not been studied.
Idh3b-null mice keep normal retinal structure and rod function to six months, whereas patients develop retinitis pigmentosa.
edges.limitations: Follow-up stopped at six months, and human IDH3B patients present in adulthood, so the model may simply not have been aged long enough; a species difference in isocitrate dehydrogenase redundancy is the alternative.

edges.description: Loss of Idh3b abolishes IDH3 activity in retina and other tissues.
edges.limitations: A complete null; the human missense alleles leave a few percent of activity and alter enzyme kinetics, which a null cannot model.

edges.description: Retinal TCA intermediates upstream of IDH3 accumulate in the knockout.

nodes.description: In Idh3b-null mouse retina, citrate, isocitrate and aconitate roughly double while alpha-ketoglutarate and the metabolites downstream of it stay unchanged, consistent with partial compensation, for example by NADP-dependent isocitrate dehydrogenases. No patient tissue metabolite data have been reported. Hartong et al. proposed that IDH2 together with the mitochondrial transhydrogenase NNT can substitute for IDH3 outside the retina, and noted from EyeSAGE expression tags that IDH3 transcripts exceed IDH2 transcripts only in the retina and retinal pigment epithelium.

nodes.description: Hypothesised link between the enzyme defect and cell loss. Photoreceptors are dependent on aerobic metabolism, and ex vivo mouse retina respires close to its maximal mitochondrial capacity with little reserve, so a partial TCA-cycle defect that other tissues tolerate could exhaust photoreceptor energy supply. Photoreceptor-specific deletion of Pdha1, which removes pyruvate entry into the TCA cycle, causes retinal degeneration in mice with decreased TCA-cycle intermediates, showing that photoreceptors need mitochondrial TCA-cycle input; that study did not involve IDH3. Direct evidence is lacking: Idh3b-null mouse fibroblasts show normal maximal and reserve respiration, Idh3b-null mouse retinas do not degenerate, and no measurement of respiration or ATP in IDH3B-deficient human photoreceptors has been reported.
